body:
> Found operating this board on 2026-09-01. The operator's own report of the session opening the human
> asked for: "there has to be a middle ground ... he does not want too much information, but enough so
> that he can start right away."

## Why

`/kanban:operate` is the first command a human runs when they sit down, and today the seat can only answer them
by hand. The prompt side of that is now fixed — `skills/kanban/SKILL.md` step 1 specifies a one-screen opening
report (board and URL, the two pids, one verdict for `doctor`, a lane table, at most three things that need the
human) — but the CLI still makes the session assemble it out of parts, and two of those parts are not available
as reads at all:

1. **Nothing prints the serve URL.** `hkb up --serve` prints `serve started pid 1122 · log .kanban/logs/serve.log`
   and `hkb up --status` prints the pid and the log; neither prints `http://127.0.0.1:4666`. The URL is the whole
   point of `--serve` and the human's way into the board, and the only way to it is the first line of
   `.kanban/logs/serve.log` — a log grep for a fact the process knows. `--port` is a flag on `up`, so the value is
   in hand at spawn time.
2. **There is no cheap "where is this board" read.** Lane counts come from `hkb list` (the whole board, one line
   per card — 29 lines here to learn that all 29 are in triage) or from `hkb stats --json`, which pays for a
   7-day attempt-and-spend history to reach `tasks.by_status`. Neither gives the priority spread within a lane,
   and neither answers the question that actually decides the opening: *is anything in flight, and what is
   waiting on a human.* An idle dispatcher and a busy one print the same status line, so with no lane read the
   report cannot tell them apart.

Both are value 4 (frictionless): the answer to "can hkb print the board's opening screen" is "yes, by hand".

## What

- **`hkb up --serve` and `hkb up --status` print the URL** for a running server, human form and `--json`
  (`serve.url`). The server already logs it; have `up` hold the origin it spawned with, and `--status` recover it
  the same way it recovers the pid. `hkb doctor`'s serve line should carry it too.
- **One board-summary read** — the shape the opening needs, from the single board query the tick already makes.
  Prefer extending what exists over a new verb: `hkb list --summary [--json]` returning counts per status, the
  priority spread per status, and the cards wearing `kb:needs-human`, with no bodies. (`hkb status <n>` is taken
  by the per-card verb, so `status` is not free as a board-level name — decide the surface before building.)
- **Keep it one read.** The opening runs `up --serve`, `up --status`, `doctor` and this one summary; anything
  that adds a second board query for the same screen has missed the point.
- Leave `hkb stats` where it is — it is the once-a-cycle spend line, not an opening.

## Done when

- [ ] `hkb up --status` and `hkb up --serve` name the URL of a running server, in both human and `--json` output.
- [ ] A single documented read returns per-lane counts, the priority spread and the needs-human cards, with no
      issue bodies in it.
- [ ] A session can print step 1's opening report from those commands without reading `.kanban/logs/serve.log`
      and without `hkb list` returning 29 bodies.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; `docs/wiki/` updated where the opening or `hkb up` is documented.
goal: hkb up --status and --serve print the running server's URL (human and --json), and one read returns per-lane counts, the priority spread and the needs-human cards with no issue bodies; the step 1 opening report needs no serve.log grep
title: The operate opening is assembled by hand: hkb up never prints the serve URL, and no read gives the board's lanes without every body
